changes.after: Use an interface to describe a method a class must provide.

before: An interface can describe behavior implemented by otherwise unrelated classes. This Reporter interface has one public abstract report() method; these modifiers are implicit on this declaration.
ConsoleReporter implements Reporter and defines public String report(). The implementation must not reduce the interface method’s public access. @Override checks the match.
The compiler checks method signatures, not whether returned text is truthful or useful. Interfaces can also have default or static methods, but this example needs only the abstract contract.

Expected output or behavior: ready
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Create a second Reporter implementation with different text and use the same calling code. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: An interface describes behavior that different classes can provide. Reporter requires a report method that returns a String. This method declaration is public and abstract even though those words are not written.

implements Reporter means ConsoleReporter promises to provide that behavior. Its report method must be public, so callers can use the access the interface promises. @Override checks that it matches the required method.

Java checks the method's name, inputs, result type, and access rules. It cannot decide whether the returned report is useful or true. Interfaces can also contain methods with bodies, but this example needs only the required operation.
The program prints ready. The call uses the report body supplied by ConsoleReporter.
The quiz removes public from the method. That would make the method less accessible than the interface requires.

before.question: Remove public from ConsoleReporter.report(). Does the interface contract still compile?
choices: No, the implementation would have weaker access
Yes, because the class is package-private
before.explanation: The method required by the interface is public. A package-access implementation cannot satisfy that public contract.

after.question: Remove public from ConsoleReporter.report(). Does the code compile?
choices: No, because the method would have less access than the interface requires.
Yes, because ConsoleReporter itself is not public.
after.explanation: The interface promises a public report method. The class must provide that public access; @Override does not add it.
